instruction: I want a technical specifications knowledge base where engineers can browse technical documents organized by modules. instruction: I want to create a webpage that implements a purely front-end-based job competency modeling and simulation system. HR professionals can search for competency models by job name or keywords, and the page will display a list of results and access detailed information. On the details page, the system needs to represent the competency model as a directed weighted graph structure, with nodes representing competencies and edges representing dependencies or reinforcement relationships. Users can directly drag and drop to adjust competency levels, modify weights, or temporarily enable/disable certain competencies. The page needs to recalculate competency coverage, critical paths, and risk competency gaps in real time after each structural change, and immediately alert users to potential problems. The system should provide a general job competency model template library, allowing HR professionals to quickly build models and save custom templates. It should also support scenario-based simulations for recruitment, training, and promotion, simulating the impact of model adjustments under different scenarios.

checklist.content: Human resources professionals can search for competency models by job title or keywords, and the system can accurately return a list of matching models.
Users can click on any model in the search results to enter the model's details page.
Users can directly adjust the hierarchy of capabilities by dragging and dropping nodes on the front end, and the model structure remains correct after layout changes.
Users can modify the weight value of any edge, and the graph will be refreshed immediately after the modification, visually reflecting the weight change.

Users can temporarily enable or disable certain capability nodes in the graph. When disabled, the node and its related edges will be visually grayed out or hidden, and will no longer participate in subsequent calculations.
checklist.bug: This function is not available.

checklist.content: The system provides a "General Job Competency Model Template Library," which users can browse and preview by job type.
Users can retrieve any template from the template library, which will be loaded as a new model into the editing interface.
Users can save the edited model as a custom template, name it, and add a description. After saving, they can retrieve it from "My Templates" at any time.
checklist.bug: My model does not exist

checklist.content: The system supports scenario-based simulation modes such as "recruitment," "training," and "promotion," and users can switch between different scenarios.
In simulation mode, users can adjust the model structure, and the system can simulate and demonstrate the quantitative or qualitative impact of this adjustment on key indicators in the scenario.
When a user leaves the page and returns, the system should be able to restore the previously edited model state, or provide an explicit save/load mechanism.
The system can prevent invalid operations that may lead to calculation errors, such as adding dependency edges to disabled capabilities.
Each time the graph structure is modified, the system can recalculate and display the updated "capability coverage" percentage in real time.
All graph structure editing operations are smooth and responsive, with no noticeable lag or delay when the model complexity is moderate.

On the details page, the system presents the competency model in a clear, interactive, directed weighted graph structure, where nodes represent competencies and edges represent dependencies or reinforcement relationships.
After each structural change, the system can recalculate and highlight the "critical path" in the model in real time.
After each structural change, the system can analyze in real time and provide a "risk capability gap" warning.
When a potential problem is detected, the system can immediately provide a clear text or icon prompt in a prominent position on the interface.
